answer_text:
Let
\[
r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2},\qquad x=r\cos\theta,\qquad y=r\sin\theta,
\]
so \(dV=r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta\).

The inequalities become
\[
0<r\le r^2 \le zr \le 2r+r\sin\theta.
\]

Since \(r>0\):
\[
0<r\le r^2 \implies r\ge 1,
\]
\[
r^2\le zr \implies z\ge r,
\]
\[
zr\le r(2+\sin\theta)\implies z\le 2+\sin\theta.
\]

Thus for each \(\theta\),
\[
1\le r\le 2+\sin\theta,\qquad r\le z\le 2+\sin\theta.
\]

The volume is
\[
V=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_1^{2+\sin\theta}\int_r^{2+\sin\theta} r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta.
\]

Evaluate the inner integral:
\[
\int_r^{2+\sin\theta} r\,dz=r(2+\sin\theta-r).
\]

Let \(a=2+\sin\theta\). Then
\[
\int_1^a r(a-r)\,dr
=
\left[\frac{ar^2}{2}-\frac{r^3}{3}\right]_1^a
=
\frac{a^3}{6}-\frac{a}{2}+\frac13.
\]

So
\[
V=\int_0^{2\pi}\left(\frac{(2+\sin\theta)^3}{6}-\frac{2+\sin\theta}{2}+\frac13\right)d\theta.
\]

Using \(\int_0^{2\pi}\sin\theta\,d\theta=0\), \(\int_0^{2\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta=\pi\), and \(\int_0^{2\pi}\sin^3\theta\,d\theta=0\), we get
\[
\int_0^{2\pi}(2+\sin\theta)^3\,d\theta=22\pi,
\]
\[
\int_0^{2\pi}(2+\sin\theta)\,d\theta=4\pi.
\]

Therefore,
\[
V=\frac{22\pi}{6}-\frac{4\pi}{2}+\frac{2\pi}{3}
=\frac{11\pi}{3}-2\pi+\frac{2\pi}{3}
=\frac{7\pi}{3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{7\pi}{3}}
\]
